name: TSA Aviation Cybersecurity
full_name: TSA Aviation Cybersecurity: HCG control set based on public TSA outcomes for airport and aircraft operators
issuing_body: Heights Consulting Group, from public announcements of the Transportation Security Administration
notice: HCG control set based on public TSA outcomes

sources.title: TSA Issues New Cybersecurity Requirements for Airport and Aircraft Operators (press release)
DHS Announces New Cybersecurity Requirements for Surface Transportation Owners and Operators (press release)
HCG TSA aviation cybersecurity control set: descriptions, guidance and test points

scoring.summary: Percentage of applicable controls assessed as in place. This is an HCG readiness measure, not a TSA determination of compliance; the client's TSA-approved security program and its SSI requirements govern.

rules.summary: A control is met only when every HCG test point under it is met.

The 2023 emergency amendment applies to certain TSA-regulated airport and aircraft operators through their security programs; confirm the client holds such a program before using this control set as a compliance gap assessment.
rules.quote: issued a new cybersecurity amendment on an emergency basis to the security programs of certain TSA-regulated airport and aircraft operators

rules.summary: Covered operators must have a TSA-approved implementation plan describing their cybersecurity measures (TSA-CIP-01).
rules.quote: The new emergency amendment requires that impacted TSA-regulated entities develop an approved implementation plan

rules.summary: Covered operators must proactively assess whether their measures are effective (TSA-CAP-01). The required cadence is set in the SSI amendment and is not stated publicly.
rules.quote: They must also proactively assess the effectiveness of these measures

rules.summary: Airport and airline operators must designate a cybersecurity coordinator and report cybersecurity incidents to CISA (TSA-GOV-01, TSA-INC-02).
rules.quote: TSA recently updated its aviation security programs to require that airport and airline operators implement the first two provisions above.

rules.summary: Cybersecurity incidents must be reported to CISA within 24 hours (TSA-INC-02).
rules.quote: report cybersecurity incidents to CISA within 24 hours

glossary.definition: Transportation Security Administration, the Department of Homeland Security agency that regulates airport and aircraft operator security programs.

Sensitive Security Information: security information TSA restricts from public release. The detailed cybersecurity requirements in airport and aircraft operator security program amendments are SSI and are not reproduced in this control set.
Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, the federal agency that receives cybersecurity incident reports.
Information technology: business systems such as email, finance and passenger-facing applications.
Operational technology: systems that monitor or control physical operations, such as baggage handling, fuel, airfield lighting and building controls.
Cybersecurity Implementation Plan: in this control set, the TSA-approved implementation plan that describes the operator's cybersecurity measures.
Cybersecurity Assessment Plan: in this control set, the operator's plan for proactively assessing whether its cybersecurity measures are effective.
